details: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) for April 2026 rose to 3.8% year-over-year, exceeding the forecasted 3.7%. This hotter-than-expected inflation data reduces the likelihood of the Federal Reserve implementing near-term interest rate cuts, which generally makes risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, less attractive. Following the report, Bitcoin and other altcoins experienced downward pressure, although Bitcoin showed some resilience by largely holding above the $80,000 mark. Higher rates typically make traditional assets like cash and government bonds more appealing compared to digital assets.
title: US April Inflation Rises to 3.8%, Pressuring Crypto Markets

details: The U.S. Senate Banking Committee released the text of a long-awaited bill (dubbed the "Clarity Act") aimed at establishing a comprehensive regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies. Key provisions include banning rewards on idle stablecoin balances that resemble bank deposits and requiring digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers to comply with anti-money laundering (AML) and customer identification requirements. The bill seeks to clarify regulatory jurisdiction over the burgeoning crypto sector, potentially boosting institutional adoption but also introducing restrictions.
title: Senate Committee Releases Crypto Bill Text, Focus on Stablecoin Yields

details: Despite the hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data, Bitcoin has managed to hold above the psychologically significant $80,000 level. This resilience is attributed to strong institutional inflows into spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), which have absorbed substantial capital in recent trading sessions. Analysts note improving on-chain activity and active buyer support, indicating robust underlying confidence in Bitcoin from institutional investors.
title: Bitcoin Sustains $80K Despite Inflation, Driven by ETF Inflows
